Definition: to be smooth (figuratively); by implication (as smooth stones were used for lots) to apportion or separate
BiblicalUsage: Chalaq means to divide, to share out. Abram divided his force by night and smote the kings, Pharaoh said he would divide the spoil, the land was divided for an inheritance by number, and God divided the sun and moon and stars to all the nations under heaven.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dividing is God's work and man's temptation in turn: He divides the land for His people and the lights for the nations, and Pharaoh divides the spoil for himself. The difference is whose hand holds the knife.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
